text_blocks.snippet: A typical roof replacement in Utah ranges from $8,000 to $25,000 or more, with an average cost of about $10,000 to $18,000 for a standard home (around a 2,000-square-foot footprint).
Installed prices vary significantly depending on the material you choose:

list.snippet: Asphalt Shingles: $4.50 – $8.25 per sq. ft. (Total: $9,000 – $16,500 for a 2,000 sq. ft. home)
Metal Roofing: $8.00 – $17.00 per sq. ft. (Total: $16,000 – $34,000 for a 2,000 sq. ft. home)
Designer / Architectural Shingles: $9.00 – $18.00 per sq. ft. (Total: $18,000 – $36,000 for a 2,000 sq. ft. home)

text_blocks.snippet: Key Factors That Impact the Price

list.snippet: Roof Size & Pitch: Roofing is priced by "squares" (100 square feet). Steeper roofs or complex angles require extra safety equipment and labor.
Tear-Off & Disposal: Removing multiple layers of old shingles increases labor time and landfill weight fees (typically adds $75 to $150+ per square).
Decking Repairs: Rotted or damaged OSB or plywood sheets found during the tear-off usually cost $60 to $80 per sheet to replace.
Local Permits & Codes: Utah municipalities generally require permits ($50 to $200) and may mandate specific ice-and-water shields or ventilation upgrades.
Location: Homeowners in metro areas like Salt Lake City or Provo can see higher localized labor quotes compared to rural parts of the state.

text_blocks.snippet: For detailed line-item breakdowns or contractor options, check out local guides such as IWC Roofing Utah Pricing Guide.
To help narrow down an estimate, let me know:

list.snippet: What is the approximate square footage or footprint of your home?
What roofing material are you leaning toward (asphalt, metal, designer)?
Do you know if your roof needs a full tear-off or has multiple layers?
